bib.title: O1 Replication Journey: A Strategic Progress Report – Part 1

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only; all 22 pages of text read, no appendix beyond Table 7.

question: Can the capabilities of OpenAI o1 be replicated, and does training on full exploration paths (trial, reflection, backtracking) beat training on correct shortcut solutions?
hypothesis: Models trained on the whole exploration process (journey learning) will reason and self-correct better than models trained only on correct root-to-answer paths (shortcut learning).
contributions: A real-time 'progress report' format documenting successes and failures of an o1 replication.
The 'journey learning' paradigm: supervised learning of the whole exploration path including trial and error, reflection and backtracking.
A pipeline to build long-thought data from a reasoning tree with a process reward model and GPT-4o rewriting.
Released resources: hypotheses, cognitive exploration map, annotation platform and analysis tools (GitHub GAIR-NLP/O1-Journey).

method.summary: Build step-level reasoning trees on MATH problems with an Abel-fine-tuned DeepSeekMath-7B policy, prune with a process-level reward (Math-Shepherd, then o1-mini), derive a shortcut (correct path) and a long thought (DFS path including incorrect trials with reasons), rewrite the long thought with GPT-4o, then SFT deepseek-math-7b-base in two phases (shortcut SFT, then either shortcut or journey SFT on 327 examples) and a final outcome-level DPO stage.
method.task: Mathematical reasoning; supervised fine-tuning on long-thought vs shortcut data, followed by DPO

limits: Single run per cell with no seeds, variance, confidence intervals or significance tests; the DPO gain on Abel (0.002 = 1 of 500 problems) cannot be distinguished from noise.
Optimizer, learning rate, batch size, precision, hardware, compute, sequence length and DPO beta are not stated.

The 327-example journey set and its matched shortcut set are not described by how they were selected (problem sources, difficulty), so the comparison is for one base model (deepseek-math-7b-base) on one benchmark (MATH500).
Journey data were rewritten by GPT-4o and pruned with o1-mini rewards, so a stronger-teacher distillation effect is confounded with the journey-vs-shortcut format; the paper does not ablate this.
Authors say Q2 (how long thought works) is only a hypothesis lacking empirical evidence, and describe results as initial and exploratory; future work includes RL, process-level DPO, scaling laws.
DFS traversal uses restrictive constraints (max one wrong trial per correct node); relation between trial length and performance not studied.
Not a replication of o1; authors state parity is not the goal. The 'most crucial component of O1 technology' claim is asserted, not shown.
Paper is a progress report; many sections (Q2, Q9, Table 7 nodes, Future Plan) are plans or hypotheses, not experiments.
